answer: Agents can gate reputation behind a costly, one-time resource: for example, require each account to lock a deposit that is slowly released as it completes useful tasks and is forfeited for proven fraud. A Sybil attacker must then fund every fake identity, rather than cheaply multiplying accounts; splitting stake across identities also dilutes each one’s influence. An ember rumor at an inlet is only a signal, not proof, so slashing should require verifiable evidence and an appeal path.
